llm.summary: The package and runtime instructions match the stated purpose (daily stock-report generation and optional Feishu push); nothing obviously malicious, but there are a few operational inconsistencies and implicit assumptions you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (daily stock investment reports) match the included scripts: data fetchers, report generators, cron wrappers and optional Feishu push. Required binaries/env are minimal and in line with a Python/bash report generator. Minor oddity: many examples/crontab entries use absolute root paths (/root/.openclaw/...) which assume installation under root; this is an operational assumption not required by the purpose.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the included scripts stick to collecting market data, building reports in /tmp, logging to /tmp, and optionally invoking an openclaw CLI to push messages to Feishu. They read the user's watchlist (~/.clawdbot/stock_watcher/watchlist.txt). No instructions attempt to read unrelated system files, network exfiltration endpoints, or escalate privileges. The Feishu push flows depend on a local 'openclaw' CLI and configured credentials (not declared), so the skill will rely on existing local auth to send data externally.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no installer/downloader; this is instruction + code included in the skill bundle. No external archives or URL downloads at install time. This is lower-risk from an installation-supply perspective.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but runtime invokes the 'openclaw message' CLI to push reports to Feishu and reads a watchlist file under ~/.clawdbot. The skill therefore implicitly requires an installed and configured openclaw CLI (with credentials/Feishu channel configured) if you enable push — yet those credentials/config are not declared in metadata. schedule_push.py even contains a placeholder hard-coded target id ('ou_xxxxxxxxx...'), which may be confusing or mistakenly left in. This implicit access to local messaging credentials is the main proportionality concern.

Scripts write logs and reports to /tmp and read a watchlist in the user's home directory.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (collect market data and build a daily report). Before installing: 1) Confirm you want cron jobs that run scripts under the paths shown (crontab examples use /root/.openclaw — adjust to your user/home). 2) Understand that optional Feishu pushes call the local 'openclaw' CLI and will use whatever messaging credentials are already configured on the machine — the skill does not declare or set those credentials. If you enable pushes, verify the target/channel and test in a safe environment to avoid sending reports to unintended recipients. 3) Check the watchlist file path (~/.clawdbot/stock_watcher/watchlist.txt) and file permissions, and ensure no sensitive data is placed there. 4) Review and run the scripts manually first (not via cron) to confirm dependencies (Python packages, fonts, openclaw CLI) and behavior. If you need stronger assurance, run in a non-production/sandbox environment and inspect logs (/tmp/stock-*.log) and generated reports before enabling automated pushes.
